claims.text: Severe plastic deformation followed by rapid quenching will induce a nanocrystalline microstructure in as-deposited FeMnNiGeSi-type HEAs.
The treatment-induced nanocrystalline microstructure will reduce magnetostructural-transition hysteresis.
The treatment-induced nanocrystalline microstructure will sharpen the magnetocaloric response.
The as-deposited FeMnNiGeSi-type alloy has an ordered, single-phase hexagonal structure.
The as-deposited alloy has a relatively coarse microstructure.
The as-deposited material has a low surface-to-volume ratio.
Severe plastic deformation followed by rapid quenching will refine the grains and increase grain-boundary density.
Thermal or thermomechanical processing can alter the magnetic state and magnetocaloric functionality of a high-entropy alloy.
Grain refinement lowers the energy barriers for the magnetostructural phase transition.
A high density of grain boundaries provides additional nucleation sites for the magnetostructural transition.
The refined microstructure decreases pinning effects at grain boundaries.
Reduced transition barriers and pinning lead to lower hysteresis losses.
The refined internal microstructure improves heat-transfer rates during magnetocaloric cycling.
Treated samples will have a smaller transition hysteresis width than the as-deposited baseline.
Treated samples will exhibit a more continuous, less sharp and less abrupt transition than the as-deposited baseline.
Treated samples will show enhanced cooling performance because of faster heat exchange.
The as-deposited baseline exhibits a large but sharp magnetocaloric entropy change.
The as-deposited baseline has high hysteretic losses.
The as-deposited baseline has limited heat-exchange rates.

The predicted effects should hold near the magnetostructural transition under low applied fields and within the material's stability window, but may vary with treatment severity or secondary-phase formation.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis says grain refinement will sharpen the magnetocaloric response, whereas the predicted outcome says the transition will become more continuous, less sharp, and less abrupt.
